\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

Layer selection is a critical, underexamined researcher degree of freedom: a biased composite metric reverses the HS advantage at 32B scale by selecting shallow layers where representation compression inflates threshold crossings. This methodological finding generalizes beyond safety probing to any threshold-dependent detection study, and the five-step audit protocol we propose (\cref{sec:discussion}) would have prevented our initial spurious scale-dependent conclusion. The empirical HS advantage is conditional: robust at 7--8B (strong for OT-7B, moderate for R1-8B), suggestive but position-mediated at 32B (moderate for QwQ-32B, qualified for R1-32B), and bounded by text encoder quality (4/4 HB against 384d MiniLM, 1/4 against 1024d BGE-large). We distinguish the methodological contribution, which is robust, from the empirical contribution, which narrows as text encoders improve. Current probes characterize the commitment phenomenon (FPR 39--52\%, oracle gap 85.5\% on R1-8B) rather than constitute production detectors; causal interventions~\citep{meng2022rome,li2024iti} and LLM-based text encoders~\citep{wang2024e5mistral} are the primary next steps.

tool_args.old_string: \paragraph{RepE inconsistency.} RepE computes the class-conditioned mean difference as a fixed direction (analytic), while LR optimizes cross-entropy to learn the classification boundary (iterative). Both require the same labeled data; the key distinction is parameterization, not supervision level. This difference is consequential: RepE mean-difference directions~\citep{zou2023representation} illustrate the metric-dependent nature of method comparison. On QwQ-32B, RepE achieves 0.756 balanced accuracy (comparable to supervised LR at 0.778), but its precision is 0.512 vs.\ LR 0.700 and its FPR is 0.309 vs.\ 0.120. The mean-difference direction captures enough signal to classify steps above chance, but fires indiscriminately on pre-CP steps, producing 2.6$\times$ more false alarms than supervised probes. On R1-32B, RepE nearly fails entirely (0.559 balanced accuracy). The inconsistency across two models sharing the same architecture confirms that a single linear direction computed from class means does not reliably capture safety commitment structure.

\paragraph{Layer selection audit protocol.}
Based on our findings, we recommend a five-step protocol for any probing study that reports threshold-dependent metrics: (1)~train probes across all layers; (2)~compute $\geq$3 metrics at each layer (at least one threshold-free and one threshold-dependent); (3)~check for metric disagreement between threshold-free and threshold-dependent selection; (4)~report sensitivity to layer choice by including results at the 2nd and 3rd best layers; (5)~compute cosine volatility (\cref{app:cosine_volatility}) as a diagnostic for crossing-rate bias at candidate layers. Steps 3--5 cost negligible additional compute and would have prevented the spurious scale-dependent conclusion in our initial analysis.

\paragraph{Layer selection audit protocol.}
We recommend five steps for probing studies with threshold-dependent metrics: (1)~train probes across all layers; (2)~compute $\geq$3 metrics per layer (threshold-free and threshold-dependent); (3)~check for metric disagreement in layer selection; (4)~report 2nd/3rd best layer results; (5)~compute cosine volatility (\cref{app:cosine_volatility}) as a crossing-rate bias diagnostic. Steps 3--5 cost negligible compute.

\paragraph{Encoder-quality boundary.}
The HS advantage is a function of text encoder quality: significant against 384d MiniLM across all evidence tiers (4/4 models$^\dagger$ HB) but attenuated against 1024d BGE-large (1/4 HB). PCA capacity matching preserves significance (+16.8 to +23.1pp), providing partial evidence against a pure capacity explanation. This boundary is itself a finding: the HS advantage represents information not yet captured by current sentence encoders rather than a fundamental modality difference. Temporal context and modality choice are complementary: at 7--8B, the modality advantage exceeds temporal improvement; temporal windowing ($W{=}3$ to $15$) provides consistent gains regardless of modality.

\paragraph{Guidance for future research.}
Robustness splits by model, not scale: OT-7B (strong) and QwQ-32B (moderate) are most stable at 5/5 seeds HB, R1-8B FPR is seed-fragile (moderate, 3/5 HB), and R1-32B (qualified) passes all seeds but its advantage is position-mediated (residualized gap NS; \cref{app:position_residual}). Distillation and native reasoning training produce qualitatively different safety representation geometry within the same architecture. PCA capacity control, control task selectivity, and position residualization (3/4 models retain significant non-positional HS advantage) provide converging evidence of genuine safety representations. Our probing approach establishes correlational evidence; causal validation via distributed alignment search~\citep{geiger2025causal}, LEACE~\citep{belrose2023leace}, or inference-time intervention~\citep{li2024iti} is necessary to confirm that probed directions are causally active in the model's safety reasoning rather than read-only features.

\paragraph{Layer selection as researcher degree of freedom.}
Layer selection is an underexamined methodological choice that can silently determine a study's conclusions. Our five-metric ablation (\cref{sec:layer-results}) demonstrates that crossing rate reverses the central finding: at biased layers, the HS advantage appears scale-dependent; at corrected layers, the HS advantage is significant across all models$^\dagger$ from strong to qualified (\cref{sec:evaluation}). \paragraph{Guidance for future research.}
The evidence gradient (strong for OT-7B, moderate for R1-8B and QwQ-32B, qualified for R1-32B) indicates that distillation and native reasoning produce qualitatively different safety representation geometry.
